; AudioInitializeAndTick: Initialize four channels at stride four using song selector $01A9, ROM stream pointers and a shared fractional tempo accumulator. The tick walks active music and effect channels; a carry-derived phase gates note processing.

; AudioAdvanceChannel: Advance the selected channel when its duration expires. Interpret stream bytes as notes or commands, retain the next stream pointer, derive pitch through the ROM period table, and update pitch modulation and envelope counters. X is channel offset 0,4,8,12; noise uses a special period conversion.

; The channel slide delay gates pitch accumulation. When its hold counter expires, clear the active amount; signed steps update the cached 16-bit period with carry rather than changing the stream pointer.
; Continue the mechanism explained at TickPitchSlide_P000256 under the same caller/register contract.

; At the sweep boundary reload the channel envelope value and reflect the countdown around $FF. Carry from the limit test decides whether to keep the old value; the shared tick commits the selected volume.
; Continue the mechanism explained at TickVolumeSweep_P000318 under the same caller/register contract.
; AudioWriteChannel: Copy cached sweep, volume and period into the APU channel selected by X. Write the high period/length byte only when it changes, avoiding an unnecessary length/envelope restart.

; AudioSelectEffect: Entry stubs choose channel X=0,4,8,12. Compare the requested effect with its current selector, then load effect header and stream. The effect countdown consumes high-nibble durations; zero terminates and restores or silences the underlying music channel.

; AudioDecodeEffect: Decode effect control and period bytes, preserving packed register fields. Advance the effect stream with carry and write changed registers. The final indirect jump dispatches music commands via a two-byte address table; command meanings are explained at their handlers.
; 41 little-endian command destinations indexed by command*2. Commands 0..40 share this dispatcher; the command byte is consumed as control, never a pointer-entry proof by itself.
; Command operands (byte counts exclude the command): 0 stop; 1 address(2); 2 release effect; 3 finish effect token.
; 4 count+address(3); 5 repeat end; 6 duration mode(1); 7 explicit note durations; 8 modulation(3); 9 modulation off.
; 10/11 signed slide(5); 12 volume(1); 13 envelope(3); 14 alternating envelope(3); 15 envelope mode off.
; 16/17 tempo replace/add(1); 18/19 transpose replace/add(1); 20 all-channel transpose(1); 21 saved envelope override off.
; 22 envelope with saved-volume override(3); 23 modulation plus explicit timer(4); 24 control+packed high-register(2).
; 25/26 repeat once/twice with address(2); 27..35 volume presets1..9; 36 default control+high-register(1).
; 37 substitution count and note(2), plus explicit duration in mode0; 38 fixed envelope; 39/40 duration modes4/2.
; Repeat state is one source/count per channel. Pitch high bytes retain packed register fields; generic tail bytes do not assert an extra musical-note domain.
; AudioStopOrRestart: Clear music activity or mask the effect selector, then rejoin stream decoding. The two adjacent entries differ in which stream they resume.

; AudioSetStreamControl: Stream commands set repeat/substitution state, note duration mode, channel control and sweep, or volume. The $0370 high bit retains an alternate envelope value; these handlers resume the same decoder rather than returning to its caller.

; Read a little-endian stream destination after the command and restart parsing there. This changes the current source without pushing a nested return; repeat commands use their separate saved source.

; AudioStreamRepeat: Read repeat count and save a return stream position, then redirect to a two-byte stream address. Later commands decrement the repeat count and either replay that address or continue after the command operands. The finite accepted stream unions retain mode/repeat-return state; wider natural song selection remains unproven.
; Initialize pitch modulation through the shared three-operand parser, then consume a fourth byte into its per-channel timer before resuming commands.
; AudioSetPitchModulation: Read modulation rate, reload interval and signed step from the stream. Seed the half-rate phase and countdown; subsequent channel ticks alternate the signed pitch step.

; The first entry disables modulation. The following positive/negative slide entries consume five operands: slide mode, amount-minus-one, hold counter, signed step magnitude and delay. Negative entry negates the step. Reload active amount and counter together so the pitch tick sees coherent state.
; AudioSetVolumePreset: Small entries select a volume preset or consume the next byte, clear envelope mode, and resume music decoding. These constants are audio controls, not game item identifiers.
; Clear the saved envelope override volume and resume the stream; it does not clear the separate envelope mode field or end the channel.

; AudioStartEnvelope: Initialize envelope mode, per-stage countdowns and step. One entry uses fixed timing; another reads timing and step bytes from the music stream. The saved volume high bit marks the envelope override.

; Set the alternating sweep mode, base value, reload count and phase, or disable it. The following tempo commands replace or add to the global tempo step, then the adjacent entry begins channel transpose handling.

; AudioTranspose: Add the next stream operand to channel transpose or reuse the saved transpose, then return to note decoding. The adjacent all-channel command installs the same transpose value into all four channel fields.
; Consume one byte into the transpose field of all four channels. It is a shared pitch-offset command, not four independent note events.

; Zero/rest plus 60descending low/high register pairs. Music notes add transpose and select these two bytes; high is ORed unmasked with cached high&$F8. Divider period+1 has the octave relation; an exact original generator is unknown.
; Four remaining patterned register bytes are generic Data. The unmasked high-byte consumer permits packed fields; this is not a pure 11bit pitch-number or harmonic-row claim.
